entries.reason: the class arrived in iOS 16, and the claim is about the release: the family it belongs to answers one question, what changed in the photo library since a moment the caller can name, and iOS 6 keeps no account of its library as of any past time. The whole of the release's library is ALAssetsLibrary and its 26 selectors, and not one of them names a moment, a revision, a count or a change: it adds an image or a video, makes an album, enumerates albums, reads an asset by URL or by group and answers the authorization (measured, the inventory printed in facts/Photos/PersistentChange.md). What the release does say when the library changes is a broadcast, ALAssetsLibraryChangedNotification at first held rung 4.0 with ALAssetLibraryUpdatedAssetsKey at 6.0, posted once per write by the library that wrote and never queued for a listener that was not there, so nothing in it can pin a moment and nothing can ask it since. The older family of iOS 8 is a different class, PHChange, whose -changeDetailsForObject: PHChange8.m already carries against that notification; the method the 16.4 header declares for this class, -changeDetailsForObjectType:error:, is of 16.0 and answers a span of time, which is what the release has no record of
entries.effect: the class is not there: NSClassFromString answers nil and alloc on a compile time reference crashes. It is also unreachable on this port from the other side: its only producers are -[PHPhotoLibrary currentChangeToken] and -[PHPhotoLibrary fetchPersistentChangesSinceToken:error:], which are absent rows in registry/Photos/ios8.json, so a caller that got one could not ask the library anything with it
